report:
Reviewed the complete interface_dependencies claim and both ordinary implementation associations, with captured body-query and method-discovery dependencies. Requirements are: the requested body consumes its own CST/signature; further reads are demanded resolution, interface, metadata, candidate and solver facts; calls may consume signatures but never callee bodies. The referenced architectural rationale clarifies that a provisional coarse input may execute extra work, while semantic dependency boundaries still stop at interfaces.

LocalFnSym::body imports self.sig, opens self.cst, constructs its own InferCtx and resolver, binds parameters from that signature, checks its own body expression, completes inference, and publishes CheckedBody. It does not request another function body. This essential entry now has the anchor association, so changes invalidate this review. ExprCst::check_with recursively visits source expressions in the same source stash. Direct local calls resolve a definition through res_to_ty/def_to_ty, obtain local.sig, instantiate FnSig and submit its parameter environment; check_call_ty uses the resulting function pointer parameter and result types. It never calls local.body. Field and constructor operations obtain field, enum, and struct interfaces; type syntax consumes signature/alias facts. Method calls delegate discovery and use the selected signature. Captured resolve_trait_method code enumerates relevant in-scope trait items, filters matching names before signature requests, classifies a fixed trait goal and then instantiates the selected function signature. These are the permitted categories of dependency. Unsupported forms recover conservatively rather than demanding a callee body. This is source inspection of the associated query and expression entry points, not an exhaustive runtime proof of every transitive provider.

The complete ordinary test clone_method_body_has_a_narrow_reusable_semantic_query_trace starts from a source string with derived Clone and checks DbDropGuard::db. Captured force_db_method requests precisely that named method body and asserts no diagnostics. The cold assertions compare the semantic metadata call list with two associated-item enumerations, the clone function signature and Clone/Sized trait signatures; they reject body-named metadata reads, assert the expected item-name lookup and establish that the requested body query executed. A second unchanged request asserts an empty metadata trace and no body-query execution. The tracing fake records these metadata categories, so this provides a concrete narrow boundary and warm reuse regression, not universal source-backed coverage for real rustc metadata or all Salsa dependencies.

The other associated test, sage_meta::todo::checking_body_interface_dependencies, is an explicit empty TODO with a concrete missing matrix: complete cold fact whitelists rejecting unrelated interfaces and callee bodies, unchanged warm reuse, and persistent edits separating relevant interface changes from unrelated body changes. It remains deferred. Completing that test requires representative fixtures and persistent-input query tracing sufficient to identify local and external dependency reads and invalidation; the existing single Clone case does not replace that matrix. No N/A entries exist. I accept this visible testing deferral without claiming comprehensive coverage.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness clone_method_body_has_a_narrow_reusable_semantic_query_trace -- --exact derive_expansion_tests::clone_method_body_has_a_narrow_reusable_semantic_query_trace: one test passed, zero failed. Ran cargo fmt after the comment-only association addition. Fresh start reviewed the updated association; the only changed source line was that comment and captured dependencies were refreshed. Workspace build and shared quality checks are coordinated separately by the parent; no behavioral change or unexecuted test is represented as validated here.
